messages:
alex: Hey @support, customer reports partial JSON on SSE after client reconnect — last event ends with a trailing comma and no finish_reason, their parser fails.

sam: Can you paste the raw SSE stream they captured?

alex: pasted below from their tcpdump (redacted token):

alex: ```
data: {"id":"act_123","choices":[{"text":"Hello"}],data: {"id":"act_123","choices":[{"text":"world"}],data: {"id":"act_123","choices":[{"text":"!"}],data: {"finish_reason": null,
```

alex: so last chunk is cut mid-object, leaving a trailing comma and no closing brace or final "[DONE]" sentinel.

maria: hmm. did the client reconnect or did proxy reconnect? any 401/502 in logs?

alex: customer says their browser detached and EventSource reopened. They saw a 200 then reconnect a few seconds later. No 401.

jordan: do we have any Fastly/edge logs showing connection reset around that ts?

infra-bot: Deploy 8823 to inference-runtime (patch for SSE flush) completed at 2312345700. No infra errors reported.

sam: Repro attempt from their steps:
sam: ```bash
# simple curl to keep-alive SSE
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=xxx\" --no-buffer
```

sam: When I CTRL-C and restart, sometimes the server emits leftover buffered chunk that looks like a partial JSON.

maria: Does the runtime send a final event like `data: [DONE]\n\n` or explicitly close connection?

alex: It should send a final data event with finish_reason. Looks like when a second connection resumes the same request id we sometimes double-emit the in-flight KV cache flush without the closing envelope.

jordan: Could be a race where prefix caching writes a token batch but the close event is dropped due to connection tear-down. Need logs with request_id.

support-agent: Customer impacted in prod; it's causing parse errors in their JS and a 1:1 support escalation. They will whitelist a workaround if we advise a client-side patch.

maria: Short-term workaround: client should tolerate trailing JSON fragments by buffering until a final `\n\n` SSE gap and then attempt safe-merge, or treat missing finish_reason as retryable and open a new request to continue. Not ideal but buys time.

sam: Example client patch (Node/EventSource):
sam: ```js
let buffer = '';
es.addEventListener('message', e => {
  buffer += e.data;
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(buffer);
    // handle parsed response
    buffer = '';
  } catch(err) {
    // wait for more chunks; if timeout, attempt safe recovery
  }
});
```

alex: Also ask them to set `Connection: keep-alive` and disable aggressive proxy idle timeouts. They were behind a corporate proxy that has 30s idle kill.

jordan: I'll add additional tracing in runtime: log SSE frames + final-sentinel emission and stash request_id. If close observed without final-sentinel, mark record for replay.

maria: Can we also ensure we always emit a final `data: {"finish_reason":"max_tokens"}\n\n` even if connection is tearing down? Maybe flush synchronously before closing socket.

infra-bot: Issue created: INF-1298 "Ensure final SSE sentinel emitted on abrupt close" and assigned to eng-runtime.

support-agent: Customer wants ETA and repro steps. They request a temporary mitigation flag on their org to send complete JSON in single event (larger payloads) to avoid stream reassembly problems.

sam: We can add an org-level toggle to aggregate full response server-side and send one final JSON event as a stop-gap. I'll prototype.

maria: Next actions: (1) eng-runtime adds synchronous final flush + logging (2) support provides client workaround snippet + recommend proxy idle settings (3) offer org toggle to send aggregated final event.

alex: Assigning to @maria for communication. Customer contact updated. :eyes:

support-agent: Thanks team — I'll send the mitigation and set expectation for INF-1298.

maria: I'll follow up here when we have a rollout plan.
